name: Diarrhea
lede: Diarrhea is a murky olive-yellow, a color named for its subject rather than for any pigment or dye.

sections.title: A name from the body
sections.body:
The books do not treat this as a color name. Finlay mentions the word while telling of a bright yellow pigment's Indian source, cow-urine yellow: she recounts stepping in cow diarrhea while in India hunting for the pigment [1]. Birren's colour-therapy chapter, summarising older healing schemes, prescribes blue over the abdomen for diarrhea and yellow for constipation, an old belief with no modern evidence behind it [2].

St Clair uses the word only for symptoms, among them those of plague and of arsenic poisoning from green dyes [3][4]. In every book the word describes illness, not a hue, so the color here is a descriptive label of olive-yellow, near [[olive]] and [[mustard]] in the screen data.

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: The swatch #9F8303 is a dark, greenish yellow [9]. Its link to the word is a naming habit of color lists, not anything the books document [1][2]. The concordance of 29 color books finds only four strong mentions of this name, so the article stays short rather than pad the record [9]. Screen colors are approximate, and the swatch is a reference value, not a measured pigment [9].
